metadata.source_file: OneStream Design and Reference Guide (online edition); each question lists source_section and source_url
metadata.note: Written from guide text for objectives 201.2.1-201.2.4, 201.5.1-201.5.6, 201.7.1-201.7.2. Not covered (pages not readable online): Designing BI Blend and Table Views Platform Guides, MarketPlace Solution, Loading Data via Excel Templates or CSV, Error Log page. Guide pages are current online versions; exam is based on 8.x.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Types
questions.question: Budget holders enter data through forms. After entry, calculations must run and confirmation rules must pass before they sign off. Which Workflow Name should be assigned?
questions.explanation: A is correct: (Form Input, Process, Confirm, Certify) is a Forms Workflow Name that runs Process (calculations) and Confirm (confirmation rules) before Certify. B is incorrect — it skips Process and Confirm. C is incorrect — the steps are right but it is an Import Workflow Name, and the input here is forms. D is incorrect — it has no Process, Confirm or Certify step.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Types
questions.question: Analysts want to import a file and review it in Stage without any data reaching the cube. Which Workflow Name supports this?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the Stage Only Workflow Names (Import Stage Only; Import, Verify Stage Only; Import, Verify, Certify Stage Only) bring data into Stage without loading the cube. A is incorrect — Load writes the data to the cube. C is incorrect — Central Import is for importing centrally, and still loads the cube. D is incorrect — Workspace presents a dashboard as the workflow step; it is not a Stage-only import.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Types
questions.question: Which of the following is a valid Workflow Name for a Journals (Adjustment) input child?
questions.explanation: C is correct: (Journal Input, Process, Confirm, Certify) is listed among the Journal Workflow Names. A is incorrect — Pre-Process options exist only for Forms, not Journals. B is incorrect — that is a Forms Workflow Name. D is incorrect — that is an Import Workflow Name.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Types
questions.question: A Workflow Profile exists only so a regional controller can review, confirm and certify the results of the input profiles beneath it. No data is entered there. Which profile type is it?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Review profiles “do not take input, but are meant for reviewing, confirming and certifying results from the lower input Workflow Profiles.” A is incorrect — Base Input is where most data updates happen (Import, Forms, Journals). B is incorrect — Parent Adjustment takes top-side adjustments into AdjInput. C is incorrect — Import is an input channel of a Base Input profile, not a review profile type.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Calculation Definitions
questions.question: When a user clicks Process Cube in a Workflow, where is it defined which entities are calculated or consolidated?

options.A: The Calculation Definitions tab of the Workflow Profile

questions.explanation: A is correct: Calculation Definitions, the second tab of the Workflow Profile, “will determine the type of calculation/consolidation that occurs when a user selects Process Cube during the Workflow.” B is incorrect — a Data Management step runs calculations outside the Workflow's Process step. C is incorrect — the algorithm type controls how consolidation works, not which entities Process runs. D is incorrect — the Confirmation Profile assigns confirmation rules, not calculations.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Calculation Definitions
questions.question: In a Workflow Profile's Calculation Definitions, what does the Confirmed check box control?

options.A: Whether the calculation runs as a Force calculation
options.B: Which entities are tested by the confirmation rules
options.C: Whether the user must confirm before Process Cube runs
options.D: Whether the entity is locked after certification

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Confirmed check box controls which entities are tested by the confirmation rules. A is incorrect — Force is part of the calculation type, not the Confirmed box. C is incorrect — there is no user confirmation prompt; the name is the trap. D is incorrect — locking after certification is the Lock after Certify setting in Application Properties.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Calculation Definitions
questions.question: Instead of listing each entity, an administrator wants Calculation Definitions to automatically include the entities assigned to the Workflow Profile. What should be used?

options.D: An Entity Filter on a Data Management step

questions.explanation: C is correct: Calculation Definitions can auto-assign entities using the (Assigned Entities) option. A is incorrect — a member filter on Root would take every base entity, not the profile's assigned entities. B is incorrect — not a real Calculation Definitions option. D is incorrect — a Data Management Entity Filter applies to that step, not to the Workflow's Process Cube.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: A user can open a Workflow Profile and see its results but cannot load or process data. Which group is the user most likely missing?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the Workflow Execution Group “is configured for data loaders and allows users to execute Workflow.” A is incorrect — the user already has the Access Group, which only allows viewing results at run time. B is incorrect — the Maintenance Group maintains and administers the profile; it does not run it. C is incorrect — the Certification SignOff Group allows sign-off, not loading.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: A team lead must be able to maintain and administer a Workflow Profile but should not load data. Which group fits?
questions.explanation: A is correct: the Maintenance Group “controls the user or users that will have access to maintain and administer.” B is incorrect — that group runs the Workflow (loads data). C is incorrect — the Access Group only views results. D is incorrect — the Journal Post Group posts journals.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: Which Workflow Profile group allows users to sign off on the Workflow?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the Certification SignOff Group “is configured for certifiers and allows users to sign off on the Workflow.” A is incorrect — it is for data loaders. C is incorrect — it approves journals, not the Workflow. D is incorrect — it only views results.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: Several entities have no activity in some months, and their users cannot finish the Workflow because nothing was loaded. Which setting addresses this?

options.B: Force Balance Accounts to YTD View = True

questions.explanation: C is correct: when Is Optional Data Load is True, the Workflow provides a “Complete Workflow” option when no data loads that period. A is incorrect — that allows loading entities not assigned to the profile, a different problem. B is incorrect — that changes the View for balance accounts. D is incorrect — NoDataLock applies to metadata members, not to completing a Workflow.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: An import fails because the file contains entities that are not assigned to the Workflow Profile. The business wants those rows loaded. Which setting allows it?

options.C: Allow Loads After Workflow View Year = True

questions.explanation: D is correct: if Can Load Unrelated Entities is False, the profile “can only load data to assigned entities”; True allows loading to unassigned entities. A is incorrect — it handles periods with no data. B and C are incorrect — both are Application Properties settings about the Workflow View and time periods, not entity assignment.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: Controllers must not be able to post journals they created, and the restriction must also apply to administrators. Which setting meets this?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Prevent Self-Post offers False, True, and “True (includes Admins)”; only the last also covers administrators. B is incorrect — it covers approving, not posting. C is incorrect — plain True does not cover administrators. D is incorrect — it only blocks free-form journals.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: Users must create journals only from approved templates, never free-form. Which Workflow Profile setting does this?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Require Journal Template “restricts users from creating new free-form journals by disabling the Create Journals button.” A is incorrect — it assigns which templates are available but does not block free-form journals. C is incorrect — it is about approving one's own journals. D is incorrect — it controls who can process journals.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Channels
questions.question: An account must not participate in any Workflow Channel grouping, so it can be used with any Workflow Profile. Which channel should be assigned to the account?
questions.explanation: C is correct: NoDataLock “only applies to a metadata Member (Account or UDx) that should not participate in a Workflow Channel grouping scheme.” A is incorrect — Standard is the default channel and still participates. B is incorrect — AllChannelInput applies to a Workflow Profile input child, not to a metadata member. D is incorrect — members default to Standard; blank is not the mechanism.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Channels
questions.question: A forms input child must be able to control data input for every Workflow Channel. Which channel is assigned, and where?

options.B: Standard, on the Workflow Profile input child
options.D: AllChannelInput, on the Workflow Profile input child

questions.explanation: D is correct: AllChannelInput “only applies to a Workflow Profile Input Child (Import, Forms or Adj) and indicates the Workflow Profile can control data input processes for any Workflow Channel.” A is incorrect — NoDataLock is for metadata members. B is incorrect — Standard only covers the Standard channel. C is incorrect — right channel, wrong place; it does not apply to metadata members.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Channels
questions.question: Two teams load different accounts into the same entity and must load, clear and lock their data independently. What enables this?

options.A: Workflow Channels assigned to the accounts and the input profiles
options.B: Separate Workflow Names for each team
options.C: Data Cell Access Security on the accounts

questions.explanation: A is correct: Workflow Channels control “data clearing, loading, and locking behaviors of the Metadata Members associated with the assigned Workflow Channel,” so each profile writes only to its own intersections. B is incorrect — Workflow Names set the steps, not data ownership. C is incorrect — that controls read/write access, not load and lock behavior. D is incorrect — transformation maps source to target members; it does not separate locking.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workflow > Workflow Profile Properties
questions.question: A file loads balance accounts on a periodic basis, but the business wants balance accounts always treated as YTD for this profile, regardless of the file. Which setting does this?

options.A: Flow Type No Data Zero View Override
options.B: Force Balance Accounts to YTD View = True
options.D: Balance Type No Data Zero View Override

questions.explanation: B is correct: Force Balance Accounts to YTD View, when True, forces YTD View for balance accounts regardless of the file. A and D are incorrect — the No Data Zero View overrides control how missing data is treated, not the view of loaded balance accounts. C is incorrect — it handles periods with no data.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Tools > Load/Extract System Artifacts
questions.question: An auditor needs the Error Log and Task Activity from Production for last quarter. Which tool provides this?

options.A: Application > Tools > Load/Extract — Application Zip File
options.B: A Data Management Export Data step
options.C: System > Tools > Load/Extract — Error Log and Task Activity, with a time range

questions.explanation: C is correct: Error Log, Task Activity and Logon Activity are System Load/Extract types, extractable by time range. A is incorrect — logs are not application structures. B is incorrect — Export Data exports cube data. D is incorrect — Security Roles is an application item and contains no logs.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Load/Extract Application Artifacts
questions.question: Which two items are NOT included when an administrator extracts the Application Zip File? (Select 2.)
questions.explanation: A and C are correct: the Application Zip File extracts “all the Application structures except for data and the FX rates.” B and D are incorrect — Cube Views and Transformation Rules are application structures and are included. FX rates can be moved separately with the FX Rates or FX Rate CSV extract types.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Tools > Load/Extract System Artifacts
questions.question: Which item is extracted with the System Load/Extract tool rather than the Application Load/Extract tool?

options.A: Security (System Roles, Users, Security Groups, Exclusion Groups)

questions.explanation: A is correct: System Load/Extract “Security” includes System Roles, Users, Security Groups and Exclusion Groups. B is incorrect — Security Roles is on the Application Load/Extract list. C and D are incorrect — both are Application Load/Extract items.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Tools > Load/Extract System Artifacts
questions.question: An administrator needs to move System Dashboards (Maintenance Units, Profiles, Components, Adapters and Parameters) to another environment. Which tool is used?
questions.explanation: B is correct: System Load/Extract has a System Dashboards type covering Maintenance Units, Profiles, Groups, Components, Adapters and Parameters. A and C are incorrect — they move application artifacts, not system dashboards. D is incorrect — Export Report renders dashboards as PDFs; it does not move them.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Load/Extract Application Artifacts
questions.question: Who can use the Application Load/Extract tool, and who can use the System Load/Extract tool?

options.A: Anyone with ManageMetadata; anyone with the SystemPane role

questions.explanation: C is correct: for Application Load/Extract, “Only Administrators have access”; for System Load/Extract, “Only System Administrators have access.” A is incorrect — neither role is the stated requirement. B and D are incorrect — the two tools have different access levels.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: A planning scenario must be wiped for a new cycle, including Workflow Status and Calculation Status, as quickly as possible. Which Data Management step fits?

options.A: Clear Data with Clear Forms Data = True
options.C: Copy Data from an empty scenario

questions.explanation: D is correct: Reset Scenario clears data, audit information, Workflow Status and Calculation Status, and “does not create audit information…therefore will run faster.” A is incorrect — Clear Data does not clear Workflow or Calculation Status. B is incorrect — it runs a calculation. C is incorrect — copying empties is slower and still leaves status behind.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: Which Data Management step clears data even when it is marked as Durable?
questions.explanation: A is correct: per the guide, “Reset Data will clear even data marked as Durable.” B is incorrect — the guide gives that warning for Reset Scenario, not Clear Data. C is incorrect — Custom Calculate writes data; durable results survive. D is incorrect — it recalculates rather than clears.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: A Custom Calculate step runs for an administrator but fails for an analyst. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The step's Point of View section is blank
options.B: The analyst is not in the Scenario's Manage Data Group
options.C: The analyst lacks the TaskSchedulerPage role
options.D: The analyst is not in the Workflow Execution Group

questions.explanation: B is correct: for Custom Calculate, the user “must be a member of the Scenario's Manage Data Group or the Step will fail.” A is incorrect — the Point of View section is optional. C is incorrect — that role only opens the Task Scheduler page. D is incorrect — that group governs running a Workflow, not Data Management steps.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: Why would an architect choose a Custom Calculate step to recalculate a small slice of data during data entry?

options.A: It creates full audit history for every affected cell
options.B: It is the only step that can consolidate
options.C: It runs a calculation on a slice of data within one or many Data Units and does not create audit information per cell, so it runs faster
options.D: It automatically clears durable data first

questions.explanation: C is correct: the guide lists speed during data entry and flexibility as the typical use, running a calculation on a slice of one or many Data Units without per-cell audit information. A is incorrect — the opposite; that is why it is fast. B is incorrect — the Calculate step consolidates. D is incorrect — Custom Calculate does not clear durable data.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: A finance team wants a Report Book generated nightly and saved to the File Share. Which step type does this?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Export File exports “an Extensible Document or Report Book to OneStream's File Share.” A is incorrect — Export Data exports cube data. B is incorrect — Export Report exports Dashboards or Dashboard Profiles as PDFs. C is incorrect — possible with custom code, but not the built-in step for this.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: An administrator wants several dashboards delivered as a single PDF on a schedule. Which step and setting fit?

options.A: Export Report with Report File Type = Combined PDF File
options.B: Export File with Process Extensible Document = True
options.C: Export Report with Report File Type = PDFs in Zip File
options.D: Export Data with Include Member Descriptions = True

questions.explanation: A is correct: Export Report outputs Dashboards as “PDFs in Zip File” or a “Combined PDF File”; one PDF means Combined. B is incorrect — Export File is for Extensible Documents and Report Books. C is incorrect — that produces separate PDFs in a zip. D is incorrect — Export Data exports cube data.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: A consolidation run from Data Management is slow, and the administrator needs more detail about where time is spent. What should be changed?

options.B: Use the “with Logging” variant of the calculation type and review Task Activity
options.C: Set Use Detailed Logging on a Clear Data step

questions.explanation: B is correct: the “With Logging” variants “trigger additional detailed logging which can be viewed in the Task Activity area.” A is incorrect — Force recalculates every cell and usually makes it slower. C is incorrect — that is a different step type. D is incorrect — it changes what runs, not what is logged.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: What does a Force variant of a Data Management calculation do?

options.A: Runs only the cells marked as needing calculation
options.C: Runs as if every included cell is marked as needing to be calculated, translated or consolidated

questions.explanation: C is correct: Force variants “will run as if every cell included is marked as needing to be calculated, translated or consolidated.” A is incorrect — that describes the normal, non-Force run. B and D are incorrect — Force does neither.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Data Management > Steps
questions.question: In a Copy Data step, the Source View and Destination View fields are left blank. What happens?

options.D: Data copies to the same View member

questions.explanation: D is correct: “If Source and Destination View fields are left blank, the data will copy to the same View Member.” A is incorrect — blank is allowed. B and C are incorrect — no fixed View is forced.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Task Scheduler
questions.question: What does Task Scheduler schedule, and what makes a scheduled job fail immediately?

options.A: Data Management sequences; a sequence that has no step
options.B: Business rules directly; a missing parameter
options.C: Workflow Process steps; an uncertified Workflow

questions.explanation: A is correct: Task Scheduler schedules Data Management sequences, and “if the sequence doesn't have a step, the job will fail.” B, C and D are incorrect — Task Scheduler runs sequences, not rules, Workflow steps or Cube Views directly.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Security Roles
questions.question: A user can create tasks but cannot edit a colleague's task. Which role allows editing other users' tasks?
questions.explanation: B is correct: ManageTaskScheduler lets users view every task and edit their own and other users' tasks. A is incorrect — an Application User Interface role that only opens the page. C is incorrect — TaskScheduler edits only the user's own tasks. D is incorrect — unrelated to Task Scheduler.

questions.subtopic: Task Scheduler — UI vs. Security Role
questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Security Roles
questions.question: A user has the TaskScheduler security role but cannot open the Task Scheduler page. What is missing?
questions.explanation: C is correct: TaskSchedulerPage is the Application User Interface role required to access the page. A is incorrect — a security role grants actions, not page access. B is incorrect — broader than needed and not the specific requirement. D is incorrect — unrelated to Task Scheduler.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Properties > General
questions.question: What does the Global Point of View in Application Properties consist of?

options.A: Company Name, Logo and Number Format
options.B: Default Currency and FX Rate Type

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Global POV is Global Scenario and Global Time, the defaults users see when looking at Workflow. A is incorrect — those are separate Application Properties sections (Company Information, Formatting). B is incorrect — default currency is a cube setting. C is incorrect — neither is part of the Global POV.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Properties > General
questions.question: Users keep changing the Workflow View to the wrong year. Which Application Properties setting prevents this?

options.D: Allow Loads Before Workflow View Year

questions.explanation: A is correct: Enforce Global POV restricts users from changing Workflow View settings. B is incorrect — Global Time only sets the default. C is incorrect — it locks after certification. D is incorrect — it allows imports to prior periods.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Properties > General
questions.question: A new entity uses Singapore dollars, but SGD is not available when setting the entity's currency. What must happen first?

options.A: Load SGD rates with the FX Rates extract type
options.B: Add SGD to the Currencies list in Application Properties
options.C: Add SGD as a member of a UD dimension
options.D: Set SGD as a cube's default currency

questions.explanation: B is correct: “All currencies used in the application must be listed here” for entity setup, translation and rate entry. A is incorrect — rates come after the currency exists. C is incorrect — currency is not a UD member. D is incorrect — the currency must exist in the application first.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Properties > General
questions.question: Where is the UD dimension that Workflow Channels can use (in addition to Account) designated?

options.C: Application Properties — UD Dimension Type for Workflow Channels

questions.explanation: C is correct: UD Dimension Type for Workflow Channels in Application Properties lets channels lock a User Defined dimension in addition to accounts. A is incorrect — that assigns a channel to a profile. B is incorrect — it enables dimensions for import. D is incorrect — that is where channel members are created, not where the UD type is chosen.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Excel Add-In > Retrieve Functions
questions.question: Which Excel Add-in function saves a value from a spreadsheet into the cube?
questions.explanation: D is correct: XFSetCell “saves data to the amount field based on the Parameters supplied.” A is incorrect — XFGetCell retrieves data. B is incorrect — it retrieves exchange rates. C is incorrect — it retrieves a description.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Excel Add-In > Retrieve Functions
questions.question: A spreadsheet needs a property from the Relationship Properties tab in the Dimension Library. Which function retrieves it?
questions.explanation: A is correct: XFGetRelationshipProperty retrieves properties from the Relationship Properties tab. B is incorrect — it retrieves from the Member Properties tab. C is incorrect — it returns True/False for whether a member has children. D is incorrect — it retrieves the description.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Excel Add-In > Retrieve Functions
questions.question: In an XF retrieve function, a field is not needed. What should be entered for that field?

options.A: Leave it out and shift the remaining fields
options.B: A double quote, to ignore it

questions.explanation: B is correct: “If a field within the function is not needed, enter a double quote to ignore it.” A is incorrect — fields are positional. C and D are incorrect — not the documented convention.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Excel Add-In > Quick Views
questions.question: Which Excel Add-in feature provides ad hoc reports that let users pivot, drill back and create data sets?
questions.explanation: C is correct: “Quick views are ad hoc reports that allow you to pivot, drill back, create data sets, and design workbooks to analyze data.” A is incorrect — functions return individual values. B is incorrect — Table Views work with relational table data. D is incorrect — Extensible Documents are formatted reports, not ad hoc analysis.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Administration > System User Interface Roles
questions.question: On which part of the System tab are File Explorer, Database, Load/Extract and Time Dimension found?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the System User Interface Roles place Database, File Explorer, Load/Extract and Time Dimension under System > Tools. A is incorrect — Administration holds security. B is incorrect — Logging holds Error Log, Logon Activity and Task Activity. C is incorrect — that is the Application tab.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Administration > System User Interface Roles
questions.question: Which three items are found under System > Logging?

options.A: Error Log, Logon Activity, Task Activity
options.C: Task Activity, Task Scheduler, Data Management

questions.explanation: A is correct: Error Log, Logon Activity and Task Activity are under System > Logging. B is incorrect — File Explorer and Database are under System > Tools. C is incorrect — Task Scheduler and Data Management are Application tab tools. D is incorrect — Security is under Administration; Time Dimension is under Tools.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Logging > Logon Activity
questions.question: A user is stuck in a session and must be logged off. Where does an administrator do this?

options.B: System > Logging > Logon Activity — Logoff Selected Session
options.C: System > Administration > Security — disable the user

questions.explanation: B is correct: Logon Activity lets an administrator use Logoff Selected Session to end any user session. A is incorrect — canceling a task does not end the session. C is incorrect — disabling the user is a security change, not a logoff. D is incorrect — unrelated.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Administration > System User Interface Roles
questions.question: A user has the LogonActivityPage role. What can they do?

options.A: View all users in Logon Activity and log them off
options.B: Only view their own logon history
options.C: View all users in Logon Activity but not log them off

questions.explanation: C is correct: with LogonActivityPage, “you can view all users, but cannot log them off.” A is incorrect — logging off requires administrator rights. B is incorrect — the role shows all users. D is incorrect — clearing activity is an administrator action.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Administration > System User Interface Roles
questions.question: A user is granted SystemLoadExtractPage. What can they do?

options.D: Open the System Load/Extract page but not actually import or extract items

questions.explanation: D is correct: SystemLoadExtractPage grants access to the page, but “you cannot actually import or extract items.” A, B and C are incorrect — a UI role grants page access, not the ability to perform the load or extract.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Logging > Task Activity
questions.question: A consolidation seems stuck. Where can an administrator see its status, duration and application server, and cancel it?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Task Activity shows Task Type, Duration, Task Status, User, Application and Server, and running tasks can be canceled there. B is incorrect — the Error Log records errors but does not cancel tasks. C is incorrect — Database is for viewing database tables. D is incorrect — that is where steps are defined, not monitored.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Logging > Task Activity
questions.question: In Task Activity, how does an administrator find which part of a multi-step task failed?

options.B: Use the icons on the left of the row to view child steps and error details
options.C: Extract the Error Log with System Load/Extract
options.D: Check Logon Activity for the user

questions.explanation: B is correct: Task Activity provides drill-down to child steps and error details through icons on the left of each row. A is incorrect — re-running doesn't diagnose. C is incorrect — extracting moves logs; it is not the first troubleshooting step. D is incorrect — Logon Activity shows sessions, not task steps.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > System Administration > System User Interface Roles
questions.question: Which System User Interface role grants access to the System tab itself?
questions.explanation: C is correct: SystemPane grants access to the System tab. A is incorrect — it grants the Application tab. B is incorrect — it allows viewing security settings under System > Administration. D is incorrect — it applies to logging on to the System Administration application.
